title: Strong shapes: triangles
examples: Teacher, why are triangles better than squares for bridges?
Can you show me how a triangle keeps things from falling down?
What other shapes are strong like triangles?

explain.say: Today we are learning about strong shapes like triangles.
Now look! Here it is in 3D: a truss bridge. Can you see the top chord and the bottom chord? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.
A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.
If you push on a square, it can easily wobble and fall.
Triangles hold their shape very well when you push them.
This is why engineers use triangles in big bridges and towers.
In real life, think about a playground slide structure.

faq.q: Why do triangles keep things from falling down?
faq.a: Triangles are strong because their three sides push against each other to keep a tight shape. You might also ask why triangles are rigid, or what makes triangles so stable.
asks: What shape is best for building?

faq.a: No, the size and the type of triangle matter for how strong it will be. You could also ask about the angles of a triangle, or which side is the longest.
asks: Does the size change the strength?
Are there different kinds of strong triangles?

faq.q: Do we use triangles in buildings all the time?
faq.a: Engineers use them in many places, not just bridges, but also in towers and roofs. You might also ask where else to find triangles, or if other shapes work sometimes.
asks: Can a square ever be as strong as a triangle?
Is this only for big buildings?

faq.q: What is the difference between a triangle and a square?
faq.a: A square has four equal sides and four corners, while a triangle only has three sides and three corners. You might also ask which shape is more stable, or how many sides they have.
asks: How many corners does a triangle have?
Which shape is better for building?

faq.q: Does the angle size matter for strength?
faq.a: Yes, the angles help determine how the forces are spread across the sides. You could also ask about right angles in triangles, or if the angles must add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
asks: How do angles affect the shape?
Must the angles add up to 180?

facts: A triangle has exactly three sides and three corners.
Triangles are very strong shapes that do not easily change their shape when pushed.
Engineers use triangles in bridges and towers to make them stable.
A square can wobble or collapse more easily than a triangle under force.

quiz.say: Which shape is best for building a tall, stable tower?
quiz.why: Triangles distribute force evenly across their three sides, making them very stable.

wrong.0: Rectangles can easily be pushed into a parallelogram shape, losing their strength.
wrong.2: Squares can push outwards and wobble if not supported on all sides.
wrong.3: Circles are strong but are not used for the main support beams in this way.

quiz.say: If a bridge uses triangles, what are they helping to resist?
quiz.why: The triangular shape locks the structure into place, resisting forces that try to change its shape.

wrong.1: Wind is only one type of force; triangles resist many pushes.
wrong.2: Gravity pulls down, but triangles also resist sideways pushes.
wrong.3: Heat affects materials, but the shape itself resists physical pushing.

quiz.say: If you build a frame using only squares, what might happen when you push on one corner?

options.show: It might turn into a rhombus or parallelogram.
options.say: It might turn into a rhombus or parallelogram.

quiz.why: Because squares have four corners, pushing on one corner allows the whole shape to skew out of its perfect square shape.

wrong.0: The structure will react to the push by changing its angles.
wrong.1: It might change shape, but it does not automatically become a triangle.
wrong.3: It might change shape, but it doesn't always break into pieces.
